html:
The Chalon were an Ohlone people of central California, living in the upper Salinas Valley and the hills around today's Soledad.

They spoke a language of the Ohlone (Costanoan) family and lived next to the Salinan to the south, the Rumsen near Monterey and the Yokuts across the hills. They gathered acorns and seeds, hunted, and burned the grasslands to keep them open. In 1791 the Spanish founded Mission Soledad on their land, one of the California missions, and most Chalon were brought into it. Disease and mission life cut their numbers sharply.
sum: The Chalon were an Ohlone people of central California, living in the upper Salinas Valley and the hills around today's Soledad.
